intro: Roof repair is the replacement or resealing of a specific failed roof component, such as a slipped tile, a perished flashing run, or a small area of storm-lifted felt, carried out without disturbing the rest of the roof structure. FixWell Services handles this kind of targeted repair across Salisbury and Wiltshire on both pitched and flat roofs, working to the safe-access standards set out in the Work at Height Regulations 2005. Call +44 7391 599 078 or use the quote form for a fixed-price assessment.

sections.heading: What Roof Repair Work FixWell Carries Out in Salisbury
sections.body: A roof repair, in handyman scope, is the replacement or resealing of one identifiable fault rather than a re-roof. FixWell replaces slipped or cracked clay and concrete tiles, matching the profile to the surrounding roof. Ridge tiles that have come loose from age or frost movement are re-bedded on fresh mortar. Lead flashing around chimneys, valleys, and wall abutments, the part of the roof most likely to fail first on a Victorian terrace, is resealed or replaced in short runs where it has lifted or split. On flat roofs, a felt blister or small puncture is patched with a matching compound. None of this touches the roof's structure, which is what keeps it inside handyman competency rather than a full roofing contract.

sections.heading: Common Roof Faults on Salisbury Properties
sections.body: Salisbury's SP1 and SP2 postcode districts hold a high concentration of Victorian and Edwardian terraces with clay or concrete tile roofs now over a century old in some cases. Their most frequent fault is a slipped tile, usually low down near the eaves where wind pressure is strongest. Flat-roof extensions and garages suffer a different problem: felt that has lifted at the edge after a storm, which needs the same-day attention we cover through our emergency handyman service if water is actively getting in. Lead flashing around older chimney stacks perishes faster than the tiles around it and is usually the first thing to fail after 60–80 years.

sections.heading: Working at Height Safely
sections.body: Every roof repair uses access equipment matched to the job: a scaffold tower for anything above single-storey reach, a roof ladder with a ridge hook on pitched tile roofs, and a harness with a fixed anchor point on flat roofs. FixWell does not carry out freehand ladder work on wet or icy tiles, in line with the Work at Height Regulations 2005. The access method is decided before the quote is given, not on the day.

sections.heading: How FixWell Carries Out a Roof Repair
sections.body: Every roof repair starts with an inspection from the ground or from a ladder to scope the exact fault before any tile is touched. The tile or flashing material is matched to what's already on the roof. The fixing method follows the fault: a slipped tile is re-nailed or re-clipped to the batten, a ridge tile is re-bedded in fresh mortar, a flashing run is resealed or replaced in a short section. Once the repair is fixed, the tiles immediately surrounding it are checked, because a fault severe enough to dislodge one tile often means its neighbours are close behind.

sections.heading: Cost and Response Time for Roof Repairs in Salisbury
sections.body: A single tile replacement typically costs £60–£150 and is usually completed in the same visit, materials included. A small flashing repair around a chimney or valley runs £80–£200 depending on access. Flat roof felt patching costs £100–£250 for a localised repair. These figures sit within FixWell's standard £20–£40 per hour rate, with fixed-price quotes available once the fault has been assessed. Storm damage that's actively letting water in gets a same-day response through the emergency handyman service.

sections.heading: When Does a Roof Problem Need a Full Roofer Instead of a Repair?
sections.body: A repair stops being a repair once the fault stops being isolated. Multiple tiles failing across a large section of roof, sagging visible from the ground, or a full re-felt of an entire flat roof all sit outside handyman scope and need a specialist roofing contractor. FixWell tells customers this clearly at the inspection stage, before any work starts, rather than attempting a patch job on a roof that needs replacing. Roof condition also forms part of FixWell's wider property maintenance service.

sections.heading: Storm Damage and Insurance Documentation
sections.body: A storm that lifts felt or dislodges tiles usually needs photographic evidence before an insurer will process a claim. Photograph the damage from the ground before any repair begins: a wide shot showing the affected area's position and a close-up of the specific fault. FixWell can provide a written description of the fault and the repair carried out, which several Salisbury customers have used to support a claim. The priority on the day is always making the roof weathertight, with paperwork following afterward.

sections.heading: Roofs, Gutters, and Wider Property Maintenance
sections.body: A roof rarely fails in isolation from the gutters beneath it. Moss and leaf debris blocking a valley gutter forces water to back up under the tiles above it, one of the more common causes of a slipped tile turning into a slow leak inside the loft. FixWell's gutter cleaning service in Salisbury clears exactly this kind of blockage, and it's worth booking alongside a roof repair rather than after, since the two jobs share the same access equipment, which keeps the combined cost down.

faqs.q: Can a handyman fix a leaking roof?
faqs.a: Yes, for an identifiable, localised leak: a slipped tile, a small felt puncture, a short run of failed flashing. The fault needs to be visible and isolated rather than spread across a large area. FixWell inspects first and gives a clear answer on whether it's a repair or a job for a specialist roofer before any work begins.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to replace a few roof tiles in Salisbury?
faqs.a: A single tile replacement typically costs £60–£150, usually completed in one visit. The exact figure depends on access (ground-floor eaves versus a two-storey ridge) and how closely the replacement tile needs to match an older, possibly discontinued profile.

faqs.q: Do you repair flat roofs as well as pitched roofs?
faqs.a: Yes. Felt and GRP flat roofs get the same targeted-repair treatment as tiled roofs: a blister or puncture is patched rather than the whole surface re-covered, provided the damaged area is small and localised.

faqs.q: Is a roof repair covered by your insurance?
faqs.a: Yes. All roof repair work is carried out under FixWell's public liability insurance, the same cover that applies to every job across Salisbury and Wiltshire, which protects your property if anything goes wrong during the work.

faqs.q: How quickly can you fix storm damage to my roof in Salisbury?
faqs.a: Same-day where the damage is actively letting water in, which routes through FixWell's emergency handyman service. A slipped tile or minor fault with no active leak is typically booked within a few days rather than treated as an emergency.
